result.title: PsyJev: Psychological Analysis via System-1 Judgment
result.summary: Self-disclosures on the Web support diverse psychological analyses, from recognizing expressed experiences to identifying symptom-relevant information. We study a shared, question-conditioned decision interface for this heterogeneous problem in content analysis. We organize PsyJudgeBench, comprising 13 annotated datasets and 82 questions across six psychological areas, while preserving source-specific criteria and masks for unobserved labels. We introduce PsyJev, a System-1 model that directly produces distributions over answers specified in each request. Joint supervised training establishes the shared judgment function, followed by Judgment-Anchored RLCD (JA-RLCD), which adapts logit-space reward optimization to heterogeneous psychological judgments through balanced supervision, selective retention of correct SFT predictions, and question-group reward optimization. The Qwen3.5-based 2B, 4B, and 9B models achieve 64.33, 66.21, and 67.56 average test F1, respectively. The 9B model exceeds the strongest external comparison by 2.54 points. Controlled 2B comparisons examine the training stages and anchored refinement. Further analyses examine question-conditioned judgment, inference cost, and probability quality, complemented by qualitative comparisons across models.

AI.brief_summary: 构建涵盖 13 个数据集、82 个问题的 PsyJudgeBench，并提出 System-1 式 PsyJev 模型，用联合监督训练加 Judgment-Anchored RLCD 直接输出问题条件下的答案分布。
AI.relevance_reason: 其绕开显式推理链的直接判断与 logit 空间奖励优化，可能为 latent 状态训练监督、答案贡献分配及 THINK/STOP 成本对照提供线索，可供核查能否迁移到多模态推理。
